problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi t\,j$ meters. Find the speed of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $2\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(7,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the velocity of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}$ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $R$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=R(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(R,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $R=7$ and $\omega =2\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =7(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(7(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+14\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the velocity vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{6},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\,i+14\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\,j \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\,i+14\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\,j \\  & =-\frac{14\sqrt{3}}{2}\,i+\frac{14}{2}\,j \\  & =-7\sqrt{3}\,i+7\,j\end{aligned}
$$
